findings.summary: POSITIVE DISPATCH ATTRIBUTION (rare for supervisor-class runs): this supervisor's ::warning:: line names both trigger and target - 'Product continuity recovery: run 32866023398 ended failure with an explicit infrastructure/control-plane signature. Dispatching Product Director/optimization pipeline on current main.' followed by the dispatched run URL https://github.com/Mickalive/Spider/actions/runs/32870361258. The origin of product-loop #6 is therefore provably this scheduled supervisor firing, closing the 'dispatcher unattributable' gap noted for cancelled-run classes elsewhere.

Recovery-policy behavior observed once: after detecting latest product-loop conclusion=failure (the marooned non-fast-forward run 32866023398), the supervisor greps that run's log against an explicit infrastructure/control-plane regex set (external_directory / Missing product_beta_architecture state / runner shutdown|lost communication / SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED / OpenCode-Ox network signatures / ECONNRESET..ETIMEDOUT / 'SPIDER control-plane overlay restoration left residue'), matched, and re-dispatched product-loop on main because authorized continuation state existed. Design intent enforced in code: a clean beta loss, audit BLOCKED or ordinary build/test failure must NOT be auto-recovered ('Supervisor refuses to hide a real product/build failure'). Which single regex matched is NOT determinable from this side of the log.

Classification opacity: the supervisor logs THAT a signature class matched but not WHICH pattern matched. Auditing why the marooned push-rejection failure (32866023398) qualified as 'infrastructure' requires grepping 32866023398's own raw log (still retained; that run is safe_to_prune=false). If that log is ever pruned, the classification rationale becomes unknowable. Suggest logging the matched pattern explicitly (joins the run-id-attributed receipt proposal CF-02).

~15s wall clock total, zero writes (Contents: read token), one gh run list sweep + one log fetch + one workflow dispatch. Negligible orchestration cost; consistent with supervisor heartbeats being cheap relative to the ~5.6 runs/hour orchestration volume concern (CF-04).
